newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ramos orders probe of Filipina's death in Japan.
newsitem.headline: Ramos orders probe of Filipina's death in Japan.

text.p: President Fidel Ramos on Sunday ordered the country's top civilian investigating body to look into the death of a Filipina entertainer at a disco in Nagano, Japan.
A presidential palace statement said Ramos gave the order to the National Bureau of Investigation after reading a newspaper report which said relatives of the girl suspected foul play.
The entertainer, Chona Lasquites, died on January 13 and her body was cremated two days later, the Manila Times newspaper said on Saturday, quoting her relatives.

The relatives said Japanese police reported Lasquites died in a fire at the disco but they said a relative, who also works as an entertainer in Japan, saw welts and bruises on the body before it was cremated, according to the Times.

The Philippines has been sensitive about the plight of an estimated four million Filipinos working overseas since Filipina maid Flor Contemplacion was hanged in Singapore in March 1995 for the killing of a Singaporean boy and another Filipina maid.

Although Contemplacion had confessed to the murders, many Filipinos insisted she was a victim of a frame-up. Her hanging triggered widespread protests in the Philippines and nearly caused a diplomatic break between Manila and Singapore.
About 40,000 Filipinas work as entertainers in Japan and there are frequent reports of them being forced into prostitution.
